commons.title: Duwamish Tribe Chairwoman (3853583066).jpg
commons.description: Cecile A. Hansen, Chairwoman of the Duwamish Tribe, speaks at the 5th Annual Duwamish River Festival. The river is part of the ancestral homeland for the people known today as the Duwamish Tribe. Local tribes have been a driving force in cleaning up the river. Visit www.epa.gov/region10/duwamish to learn more about EPA's efforts to clean up and restore the lower Duwamish River.
commons.editorial_reason: Duwamish-linked speaker at a festival, but the image shows ordinary modern clothing and no visible cultural practice or object.

commons.title: James Rasmussen 01.jpg
commons.description: James Rasmussen (Duwamish Tribal member and director of the Duwamish River Cleanup Coalition, author of afterword) participating in author reading/talk for Once and Future River: Reclaiming the Duwamish, Town Hall Seattle, Seattle, Washington, U.S.
commons.editorial_reason: Portrait of a Duwamish member at an author talk; ordinary modern setting and clothing with no cultural content.

commons.title: Tom Reese, James Rasmussen, Eric Wagner, Lynda Mapes.jpg
commons.description: Author reading/talk for Once and Future River: Reclaiming the Duwamish. Left to right: Tom Reese (photographer), James Rasmussen (Duwamish Tribal member and director of the Duwamish River Cleanup Coalition, author of afterword), Eric Wagner (wrote the essay that makes up much of the book), Lynda V. Mapes (moderator, environmental reporter at the Seattle Times), Town Hall Seattle, Seattle, Washington, U.S.
commons.editorial_reason: Modern author panel with no visible Duwamish cultural dress, craft, performance, or objects.

commons.title: Salmon Bay Charlie's home, ca. 1900 - DPLA - a1720e3dfbc3bffa2abf9e108fde2583.jpg
commons.description: Transcribed from photograph: "Seattle Houses. Salmon Bay Charlie['s Home']. Exterior. Three-quarter view of front from left side. Shack home of character in pioneer days." According to Paul Dorpat's October 12, 2003 article in the Seattle Times' magazine 'Pacific Northwest,' the home was located near the base of W. Sheridan St. on Shilshole Bay.
commons.editorial_reason: Historical shack attributed only to Salmon Bay Charlie; caption does not specifically establish Duwamish identity or cultural content.

commons.title: Tilikum Place, 1975 (51577130026).jpg
commons.credit: Seattle Municipal Archives from Seattle, WA
commons.description: Richard W. Belmont, Jr., Chairman Suquamish Tribal Council; Myrtle Loughrey Lawson; Professor Willard Bill, Chairman Duwamish Tribal Council and Director/Lecturer at Center for Indian Teacher Education, University of Washington. They are standing in front of the statue of Chief Seattle at Tilikum Place near the corner of Fifth and Denny in Seattle.
commons.editorial_reason: Modern group portrait with no visible Duwamish cultural content; standing near a statue is insufficient.
